description: Two colonies with identical rules and identical rank, and one difference: Mortal Mirror's cells die of old age, while Conway's Classic never ages. The dish starts as an exact mirror image, so what pulls the two sides apart is mortality (plus a coin flip wherever both claim the same empty cell).

organisms.name: Conway's Classic
organisms.description: The original Game of Life rules: a cell is born with exactly 3 neighbors of its own kind and survives with 2 or 3, otherwise it dies. It can only defend, never take a cell from another organism, so in a mixed dish watch invaders eat into its colonies.

payload.summary: Born on an empty cell with exactly 3 neighbors

organisms.name: Mortal Mirror
organisms.description: A mirror image of Conway's Classic with one change: its cells die of old age. Birth and survival work the same way, so any difference between the two sides comes from mortality.

payload.summary: Dies of old age after 10 cycles
Born on an empty cell with exactly 3 neighbors of its own kind
Survives with 2 or 3 neighbors of its own kind

battles.name: Short Lives
battles.description: The same mirror image on a compact 50x30 dish. Less room means the two sides meet sooner, and the mortal side thins out quickly.

battles.name: Mirror Match
battles.description: Blue Conway's Classic on the left, amber Mortal Mirror on the right, starting as exact mirror images. Watch the amber side thin out as its cells age and die while the blue side keeps its ground.
